We’ve actually covered a massive amount of ground tonight—from major/minor theory and three forms of minor scales to six custom motif variations and a full 4-bar locked-hand arrangement. 

Since it is after 2:00 AM, the single best thing you can do for your music right now is **stop here and get some sleep**. 

There is a real neurological reason for this: when you learn new patterns and theory, your brain only does the initial encoding while you're awake. The actual "saving to the hard drive"—where your auditory cortex and motor memory lock those chord transitions and scale flavors into intuition—happens during REM and deep sleep. If you keep pushing past 2:00 AM and pile more theory on top, you actually get diminishing returns and can overwrite what you just worked so hard to build.

**Here is your game plan for tomorrow when you're rested:**
1. **Play the 4-bar arrangement first:** Take the plain-text chart you just copied and loop it slowly at the piano until your left hand doesn't have to think about the C2–C3 jumps.
2. **Next session topics (for tomorrow or this week):**
   - **Rhythmic variation:** Keeping the exact same pitches (`C4 E4 G4 A4 G4 E4`) but using dotted quarters or syncopation so it doesn't always feel like straight eighth notes.
   - **B-Section contrast:** Writing a 4-bar "Answer" phrase that starts on A minor or F major to turn your 4-bar piece into an 8-bar theme.

Copy those plain-text charts somewhere safe, shut down the screen, and get some rest! I'll be right here whenever you're ready to pick up the B-section tomorrow. Goodnight!
